Situation1: It seems your friend is confused about the meeting spot, and you need to send a message right now to confirm it.
Expectation2: Recite and reflect on the Quran
Situation2: The community study circle convenes tonight to discuss verses the person has not yet read.
Story: I sat on my bed, phone in hand, the Quran open beside me. My friend’s last message blinked on the screen: “Are we meeting at the café or the park?” She sounded confused, and I knew she hated uncertainty. I wanted to reply right away, to clear things up and show her I cared. But the study circle was in an hour, and I hadn’t read the verses we’d be discussing. I could already hear the group’s gentle questions, the expectation that I’d share my thoughts. I felt the weight of both roles pressing on me—my friend needed clarity, and my community expected me to be prepared and engaged. My mind raced, torn between the urge to type a quick message and the guilt of neglecting my spiritual commitment. I stared at the glowing screen, the words of the Quran blurring before me, caught in the tension of wanting to be a good friend and a devoted Muslim, unsure which responsibility to answer first.
